title: A new method for concomitant evaluation of drug combinations for their antimicrobial properties
author: Rizvi, Chowdhury, et al.

steps.title: Prepare concentrated TSB media
steps.instruction: Prepare Tryptic Soy Broth (TSB) at 1.33 × the normal concentration and sterilise it.

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic stock solutions (biofilm)
steps.instruction: For each standard antibiotic, calculate the stock concentration as Ss = 20 × a × n µg ml⁻¹ (a = required concentration in µg ml⁻¹, n = number of standard antibiotics) and prepare the corresponding stock solutions.

steps.title: Prepare test‑compound stock (biofilm)
steps.instruction: Make a stock solution of the test compound in sterile saline or an appropriate solvent with concentration St = 40 × b µg ml⁻¹ (b = desired concentration in the first well). Example: for b = 512 µg ml⁻¹, St = 20 480 µg ml⁻¹.

steps.title: Inoculate TSB with test isolate
steps.instruction: Inoculate fresh TSB with a single colony of the test isolate, then incubate overnight at the appropriate temperature.

steps.title: Dispense TSB into assay plate (biofilm day 2)
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of TSB to all required columns of the microplate and add 90 µl of TSB to the first column.

steps.title: Add test compound and serial dilute (biofilm)
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl of the test‑compound stock solution to the first column, then perform a serial dilution across the plate to obtain the desired concentration series.

steps.title: Prepare standard‑antibiotic cocktail (biofilm)
steps.instruction: Dilute each standard‑antibiotic stock in sterile saline to obtain a final concentration of “b” µg ml⁻¹. Use the relation vs = Vtotal × 5 × n; for a 1 200 µl final cocktail with n antibiotics, add 120 µl of each antibiotic to 1 080 µl saline.

steps.title: Add antibiotic cocktail to wells (biofilm)
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of the prepared cocktail to the appropriate wells to achieve the target concentrations of each standard antibiotic.

steps.title: Add diluted test culture (biofilm)
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of a 1:1 diluted test culture (mixed with TSB) into each well.

steps.title: Incubate biofilm plate
steps.instruction: Seal the plate and incubate at 37 °C for 48 h without shaking.

steps.title: Wash and stain biofilm (day 4)
steps.instruction: Decant media and wash wells three times with 200 µl of 1× PBS (pH 7.4).

steps.title: Add crystal violet and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl of 0.1 % crystal violet solution to each well and incubate for 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Ethanol extraction and read absorbance
steps.instruction: Wash wells twice with PBS, then add 200 µl of 95 % ethanol. Record the absorbance of the ethanol‑solubilised stain at 590 nm.

steps.title: Analyze biofilm OD values
steps.instruction: Compare the obtained OD590 values with the positive control (strong biofilm former) and the negative control (TSB alone).

steps.title: Prepare concentrated MHB media
steps.instruction: Prepare Mueller‑Hinton Broth (MHB) at 2 × the normal concentration and sterilise it.

steps.title: Inoculate MHB to 0.5 McFarland
steps.instruction: Add 1 part overnight culture to 300 parts fresh MHB to obtain a 0.5 McFarland suspension (≈0.1 OD at 600 nm).

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic stock solutions (MIC)
steps.instruction: For each standard antibiotic, calculate the stock concentration as Ss = 10 × a × n µg ml⁻¹ (a = required concentration, n = number of antibiotics) and prepare the stocks.

steps.title: Prepare test‑compound stock (MIC)
steps.instruction: Make a stock solution of the test compound with concentration St = 20 × b µg ml⁻¹ (b = desired concentration in the first well). Example: b = 512 µg ml⁻¹ → St = 10 240 µg ml⁻¹.

steps.title: Dispense MHB into MIC plate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of MHB to all required columns and 90 µl of MHB to the first column of the microplate.

steps.title: Add test compound and serial dilute (MIC)
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl of the test‑compound stock to the first column and serially dilute across the plate.

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic cocktail for MIC
steps.instruction: Dilute each standard‑antibiotic stock in sterile double‑distilled water to reach the final concentration “b” µg ml⁻¹. Use vs = Vtotal × 5 × n; for a 1 200 µl cocktail with three antibiotics, add 120 µl of each antibiotic to 1 080 µl water.

steps.title: Add antibiotic cocktail to MIC wells
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of the cocktail to the appropriate wells to obtain the desired antibiotic concentrations.

steps.title: Add diluted bacterial culture (MIC)
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl of a 1:100 diluted secondary bacterial culture to every well.

steps.title: Incubate MIC plate
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 16–20 h (or 14–18 h depending on the organism) at 37 °C.

steps.title: Measure MIC absorbance
steps.instruction: Record the absorbance at 600 nm using a microplate reader to determine the minimum inhibitory concentration.

steps.title: Validate assay with chloramphenicol combo
steps.instruction: Transfer fresh MHB (100 µl) into each well, serially dilute chloramphenicol starting at 100 µg ml⁻¹, add trimethoprim (0.02 µg ml⁻¹) and kanamycin (0.3 µg ml⁻¹). Add 10 µl bacterial culture (OD 0.1) to each well, incubate 14–18 h at 37 °C, then measure OD at 600 nm. No change in OD (MIC89) indicates no interaction.

steps.title: Validate assay with sulfamethoxazole combo
steps.instruction: Transfer fresh MHB (100 µl) into each well, serially dilute sulfamethoxazole starting at 100 µg ml⁻¹, add trimethoprim (0.06 µg ml⁻¹) and kanamycin (0.98 µg ml⁻¹). Add 10 µl bacterial culture (0.5 McFarland) to each well, incubate 14–18 h at 37 °C, then measure OD at 600 nm. Significant OD change (MIC89) shows antimicrobial activity of the combination.

steps.title: Calculate percent inhibition
steps.instruction: Use the formula MICₓ,ₓ = [(Control OD − Test OD) / Control OD] × 100 to express inhibition as a percentage.
